text:
HTTPS is the first line of defense for any website. It encrypts data between the user's browser and the server, so hackers cannot read passwords or credit card numbers. However, security goes beyond encryption. Authentication ensures that only approved users can access sensitive areas, often using strong passwords and two-factor verification.

Even with HTTPS, common vulnerabilities lurk in poorly written code. For example, SQL injection happens when attackers insert malicious commands into input fields. Input validation stops this by checking that all user data matches expected formats—like rejecting letters in a phone number. Similarly, cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks can be blocked by escaping special characters. Remember: secure coding is a habit, not a one-time fix.
